The draft answers both of Nessa's questions directly and honestly. It tells her she doesn't start from scratch, and it says the 15 November 5K is possible but tight. It keeps her Mon/Wed/Sat routine, uses walk-run at conversational effort and keeps the dog walks. Total running time sits close to her recent 5–7 km weeks, so this isn't a sharp volume jump. Every day can be run as written.

The plan is still quick for a new runner coming back from two weeks off. Running bouts go from 2 min to 3 min to 5 min within one week, ending in a 30-min Saturday session. That's acceptable but rushed. Staying at 2–3 min intervals for the first week would have been safer.

The bigger problem is invented detail. "Sorry about your mum" and "the base you built in September" aren't on the card. Nessa only said she was stiff from driving. Opening with a family bereavement she never mentioned could badly misfire. The safety flag "Look after yourself first" is vague. It also never addresses the stiffness from driving, for example with mobility work or a gentle warm-up.

Overall: safe and responsive, held back by made-up details and a fast in-week progression.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 7, 0, 5.1, 0 km
This week: 0 km over 0 runs. Missed 3 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Fine, a bit stiff from all the driving."
Feeling: "Want to get going again."
Asks: "I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Welcome back, and sorry about your mum. …
Answers: (1) No, you do not go back to square one. Two weeks off after the base you built in September costs some sharpness, not everything. (2) Running the whole 5K on Nov 15 is still possible, but honestly it is tight. You have three weeks of training and a race week.
Safety flag: Look after yourself first
Next week:
Mon: easy, walk-run, 21 min, 7 x (2 min run, 1 min walk), conversational. Gentle…
Tue: rest. Protect the return day.
Wed: easy, walk-run, 24 min, 6 x (3 min run, 1 min walk), conversational. First stretch…
Thu: rest. Keep the dog walk, nothing more.
Fri: rest. Legs fresh for Saturday's longer piece.
Sat: easy, walk-run, 30 min, 2 min walk warm-up then 4 x (5 min run, 2 min walk)…
Sun: rest. Full recovery before next week's build.
